scope.reason: The rebuild tree src_new/ + tests_new/ is the product being cleaned, ahead of the src_new -> src cutover. The legacy src/ and tests/ trees are slated for deletion once the rebuild is fully working and are kept only for reference, so they are readable to explain why a rebuild module ports an odd behaviour, but are never swept and never filed against. docs/audits/ is sealed rather than referenced: it holds nine prior findings reports, and a sweeper that reads one has stopped being blind, which makes the pass compromised by definition. Both ledgers are sealed for the same reason. The governance artifacts (project description, requirements, user stories, architecture) are readable because activities 0 and 2 exist to compare the code against them. tmp/ is scratch and never a product.

0.title: Specs — requirements and user stories exist, are testable, and cover the code

passes.direction_note: Reconnaissance only — no source or test file was touched.
passes.note: Seed reconnaissance sweep — one subagent, briefed on the full flag catalogue and the whole scope, deliberately shallow and time-boxed. Returned 22 findings across 12 flag classes and reported no contamination. This is a sample, not an inventory: it satisfies no gate and makes no completeness claim. Its only purpose is to give every activity a non-empty denominator, so that activity 0's and 1.a's verification is not vacuous by construction. Findings carry the sweeper's own confidence rating and are unverified — each is checked under Phase 2.5 by the activity that owns it, before any fix.

Pass 1 swept the code->spec direction blind and returned 25 spec-gaps across 12 subsystems, but rediscovered NEITHER item in the frozen denominator. Both misses are the same class, and it is a class the brief did not ask for: the sweeper hunted BEHAVIOUR WITH NO REQUIREMENT and found it well, but never looked for requirements that contradict EACH OTHER, or that fall silent on a state the system can actually reach. CD-0001 is two acceptance criteria of one story disagreeing about the same event; CD-0024 is an acceptance criterion saying nothing about a reachable case. Neither is 'undocumented behaviour', so neither was in scope for how the sweep was framed. Pass 2 brief: read each story's acceptance criteria AGAINST EACH OTHER and against the requirements they cite, and for every criterion ask which reachable states its Given clause fails to cover. Method guidance only — name no locations.
passes.direction_note: Analysis only; activity 0 changes no code. No source or test file touched.

passes.note: Pass 2 hunted the shapes pass 1 could not see — criteria contradicting each other, and criteria falling silent on reachable states — and returned 20, most of them genuine and several severe. It still rediscovered NEITHER denominator entry, so two full passes have now missed the same two items and activity 0 remains uncertified. The near-miss is informative: pass 2 analysed the SAME RULE as CD-0001 (US-11 AC-9's vanish threshold) and reported its other side — bulk deletion being refused — without ever crossing that criterion against the one governing a tool that returns. Both passes reasoned about rules in the abstract; neither ENUMERATED THE STATE TRANSITIONS AND EVENT ORDERINGS the system can undergo and walked each against the spec. Both misses live in a sequence rather than in a rule: present -> absent -> present-but-empty, and origin-holds-special-state -> origin-loses-a-race. Pass 3 brief, if run: adversarial — assume the defect class is present; build the state machine the system actually has, enumerate every transition and every two-event ordering within one poll, and ask of each what the spec says. Method only; no locations, no counts, no expectations.
passes.direction_note: Analysis only; activity 0 changes no code.

passes.note: Adversarial tier, three fresh concurrent sweepers with different framings, per the protocol's pass-3 depth. All three attack SEQUENCES rather than rules, because both surviving misses live in a sequence and two passes that analysed rules in the abstract walked past them: (a) enumerate the state machine a tool and an artifact actually have and walk every transition against the spec; (b) enumerate two-event orderings inside one poll window; (c) trace the lifecycle of state that belongs to one tool or surface rather than to the artifact, through every operation. This is the last pass the protocol allows; if the misses survive it, that is the reported answer.

sweeper_events.how: The sweeper ran `grep -rn "<term>" src_new tests_new docs`. The bare `docs` directory argument reached docs/out_of_activity_ledger.json, docs/architecture_implementation_plan.md and a file under docs/audits/, and their matching lines were rendered into its context.
sweeper_events.what_leaked: Not adjacent context — the answer key for that sweeper's own assigned defect class. It saw a ledger entry naming the exact per-tool state, the operation that drops it, and the 'owner is not the source' framing, which is one of the two entries in this pass's denominator. It also saw a plan row naming the single fix site and all four call sites.
sweeper_events.root_cause: The BRIEF, not the agent. It listed forbidden files by name but permitted the four specification files under docs/, and never anticipated a directory-level tool argument reaching siblings. Naming files to avoid does not constrain a recursive search rooted above them.
sweeper_events.remedy: Output discarded in full; none of its observations filed on its authority. Re-run with a fresh agent under a tightened brief: recursive search permitted ONLY over src_new/ and tests_new/, every specification file opened by exact path, and docs/ never passed as a directory nor enumerated.
sweeper_events.salvaged: One lead it listed as established BEFORE the leak, and which the leaked material did not concern, was re-derived and verified from scratch by the orchestrator and filed on that evidence as CD-0071 and CD-0072. It is credited to the orchestrator, not to a sweep, and counts toward no rediscovery.

defects.title: Per-tool availability tracking was dropped as YAGNI, orphaning the four spec items written in terms of it
defects.evidence: The rebuild keeps only a per-poll integer: count_available_tools(resolved_paths, definitions) returns how many tools are available NOW (sync_once.py:42-59). No per-tool status is carried in SyncState across polls, so no transition can be observed. The drop was deliberate — docs/architecture_implementation_plan.md records 'Per-tool availability-status transition logging — old tool_status.py logged available/unavailable/disabled transitions; the new tree keeps only count_available_tools (the two-tool guard's consumer). Dropped as YAGNI; document the reduced observability. [decision: drop]'. But four spec items are written in terms of that state: US-11 AC-2 ('Given an agentic_tool's status was available at the previous poll and its directory has become missing'), AC-3 ('Given ... was unavailable at the previous poll and its directory is present ... at the current poll'), AC-5 (status-transition logging), and NFR-12 ('The daemon shall log an agentic_tool's status only on transitions (startup counts as a transition), not on every poll'). US-11 also carries a five-column status table (Configured / Enabled / Root reachable / Logged on entry) describing a per-tool status model the rebuild does not have.
defects.impact: The drop was assessed as costing observability. It cost more than that: it removed the state three acceptance criteria and one NFR are phrased against, so those items cannot be implemented or verified as written — they are not merely unbuilt. This is the root of CD-0001: US-11 AC-3's re-extension rule needs to know a tool just returned, and nothing knows that. Resolving CD-0001 by tuning the glitch threshold would paper over a missing concept; resolving it by restoring availability tracking reopens a decision recorded as closed. Either way it is the spec owner's call, not an implementation detail.

defects.title: Archive GC permanently deletes preserved user bytes on a hard-coded age/rate schedule
defects.evidence: KEEP_ALL_WITHIN_DAYS=7, DOWNSAMPLE_DAYS=30, RETAIN_DAYS=365, KEEP_PER_DAY_RECENT=4, KEEP_PER_DAY_OLD=1 (lines 37-41). _apply_tiered_policy -> `else: to_delete.append(entry)` (198); _remove_entry: `if path.is_dir(): shutil.rmtree(path) else: path.unlink()` (229-233). Asserted by test_artifact_archive.py::test_entries_beyond_retention_are_deleted and three siblings.
defects.impact: NFR-07 bounds archive growth by restricting CREATION only; it says nothing about deleting entries legitimately created. US-05 AC-2 requires files be 'moved to archive — never rm'd' and makes the archive the recovery mechanism. No requirement authorises destroying archive entries or sets 7/30/365 days or 4/1 per day. The guarantee the project sells hardest — no user content is ever destroyed — is silently time-limited by five unagreed constants.

defects.title: The daemon voluntarily exits after five consecutive failed polls
defects.evidence: DEFAULT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 5, commented 'this many consecutive ones in a row downs the daemon (FR-02)'; watch: `consecutive_exceptions += 1 ... if consecutive_exceptions >= max_consecutive_failures: return EXIT_RUNTIME_FAILURE` (88-95).
defects.impact: FR-02 is cited but is about fault isolation BETWEEN artifacts and tools — it authorises continuing, never stopping. US-07 AC-3 requires the daemon resume 'without operator intervention'; NFR-04 and NFR-17 agree. NFR-10 defines a distinct runtime-failure exit code but never says what triggers it. At the 2s default interval a recoverable condition kills the unattended daemon in ~10 seconds.

defects.title: Hard input-size caps refuse and freeze legitimate artifacts, and are explicitly non-configurable
defects.evidence: MAX_PARSE_BYTES=16MiB, MAX_FRONTMATTER_BYTES=256KiB, MAX_SKILL_AUXILIARY_FILES=1000, MAX_SKILL_FOLDER_BYTES=32MiB, MAX_YAML_ALIAS_RESOLUTIONS=10000 (33-53). Module docstring: 'The bounds are deliberately constants, not configuration.' ParserBoundsExceeded subclasses MalformedSurfaceError so the read phase records a ParseFailure -> FreezeArtifact.
defects.impact: No FR or NFR mentions input size or DoS resistance. FR-11 authorises freezing when metadata is MALFORMED; a 40MiB well-formed skill folder is not malformed. A large but legitimate skill (reference PDFs, a dataset sample) is excluded from sync forever, reported only as a freeze. Five thresholds decide what the product will sync, with no requirement behind them.

defects.title: Writing one MCP slot rewrites the whole shared config file, destroying the user's comments
defects.evidence: Module docstring: 'Round-trip preserves key order and data; it does not preserve comments.' serialize re-emits the whole deserialized root via json.dumps or the hand-rolled _emit_toml_table (48-56); keyed_map_slot.write_slot calls it on the whole root (94).
defects.impact: US-01 AC-5 forbids exactly this: 'existing key order, comments, and quoting style are preserved where the underlying format permits' — TOML permits comments. US-04 AC-4 repeats it for renames; the integration protocol requires keys outside map_key_path be preserved byte-for-byte. The markdown dialect honours this via a ruamel round-trip loader; this codec does not. The user's own annotations in ~/.codex/config.toml — a file agents_sync does not own — are deleted, and only the slot fragment is archived.

defects.title: Cursor is declared to support agent and skill, which US-13 explicitly denies
defects.evidence: VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR. cursor.py declares five recipes including SurfaceRecipe('agent', 'cursor_agents_dir', ..., Layout.DIRECTORY) at line 29 and SurfaceRecipe('skill', 'cursor_skills_dir', ..., Layout.SKILL_FOLDER) at line 60. US-13 line 45 reads: "Cursor's adapter ships with `rules`, `slash_command`, and `mcp_server` support — no `agent`, no `skill` — because Cursor has no file-based equivalents for the latter two." US-10 AC-3's worked example lists cursor as {rules, slash_command, mcp_server}.
defects.impact: The daemon materialises the user's entire agent and skill library into two directories the spec says Cursor cannot read: dead files on disk, doubled write and archive volume for every agent/skill change, and Cursor added to every conflict and tiebreak group for types it does not consume.

defects.title: A from-scratch global-rules file is created under AGENTS.md, not the tool's create-name
defects.evidence: VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR. read_tool_surfaces.py:373-375: `# FR-10: a rules file that does not exist yet is created under the highest-precedence declared filename (``AGENTS.md`` where offered). return resolved.path / recipe.candidate_filenames[0]`. claude.py declares candidate_filenames=('AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md'). US-14 AC-5 — marked [x] DONE — requires the opposite: 'the file is created under that tool's create-name (the lowest-precedence / legacy standard name: CLAUDE.md for claude, AGENTS.md for codex and opencode)'. FR-10 governs DETECTION precedence, not creation, so the comment misattributes its own rule. SurfaceRecipe has no create-name field at all.
defects.impact: A fresh Claude Code install receives its synced global rules at a filename Claude may not load, so the rules appear to sync but have no effect — the precise failure US-14 AC-5 exists to prevent. The create-name concept has also been dropped from the data model, so there is currently no way to express it.

defects.title: Tool availability is 'any one directory exists', and reachability is judged again, differently, per kind
defects.evidence: `if any(directory.exists() for directory in directories): available += 1`. Contrast reconcile_known.py:150-176 _has_vanished_surface, whose docstring says judging per tool 'would not do'. Two coexisting definitions of reachable.
defects.impact: US-11 AC-1 defines the opposite quantifier — a tool is unavailable when ANY of its configured directories is missing. The safety count gating every destructive operation (US-07 AC-5) is computed by a rule the spec inverts, so a half-uninstalled tool inflates the available count and re-enables destructive polls. Overlaps CD-0025 (no per-tool status exists at all).

defects.title: The canonical rewrites user content: CRLF to LF, trailing newlines collapsed, fields stripped, tool lists sorted
defects.evidence: canonical_store.py:174 persists document.normalised().to_dict(). normalised(): name=self.name.strip(), description=self.description.strip(), body=_normalise_body(self.body), tools=tuple(sorted(self.tools)), disallowed_tools=tuple(sorted(...)). _normalise_body: replace CRLF/CR with LF, rstrip newlines, then add exactly one. Pinned by test_canonical_document.py::test_body_line_endings_normalised_to_lf_with_single_trailing_newline.
defects.impact: NFR-06 requires round-tripping 'preserve the original bytes on the source'; NFR-16 requires reading into canonical form 'shall not lose user-authored information'; US-01 AC-5 requires preserving formatting on rewrite. On Windows (first-class since v0.3) every synced artifact is silently converted to LF, showing up as a whole-file diff in the user's own version control. Sorting a tools list changes semantics for any tool treating order as precedence. Note auxiliary_files explicitly exempts itself from newline normalisation; the document body has no such exemption written anywhere.

defects.title: Skill rename rmtrees the old folder having archived only SKILL.md; skill removal orphans the folder
defects.evidence: Independently found by this sweep as a SPEC gap; the same code is already filed as a defect (CD-0012 rename, CD-0013 removal, CD-0017 docstring). The spec angle is new: US-05 AC-2 requires that on removal 'each other agentic_tool's file OR FOLDER is moved to archive — never rm'd', and US-01 AC-9 makes auxiliary files first-class synced content, so the archive scope and the delete scope of a folder-layout artifact are specified and the code matches neither.
defects.impact: Corroborates CD-0012 from the spec direction and supplies the requirement the fix must satisfy. No requirement permits rmtree of unarchived bytes, nor an orphaned folder after removal.

defects.title: An unreadable file or transient I/O error on one tool freezes the artifact on every tool
defects.evidence: `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, MalformedSurfaceError) as error: return SurfaceObservation(..., parsed=ParseFailure(f'unreadable surface: {error}'))` (214-219); reconcile_known.py:60-61 turns any single ParseFailure in the group into FreezeArtifact for the whole artifact.
defects.impact: FR-11 authorises freezing exactly one case: 'When the metadata is malformed such that content cannot be parsed'. A permission error, a mid-write partial read, or an oversize file is not malformed metadata. US-03 AC-11 scopes freeze the same way; US-07 AC-3 and FR-02 point the other way for I/O errors. One antivirus lock stops that artifact syncing on all tools.

defects.title: An `agents-sync prune` subcommand exists and the daemon runs an archive GC every 24 hours
defects.evidence: subcommands.add_parser('prune', ...); _dispatch routes it to _prune(config); run_daemon passes run_gc=lambda: _gc_once(state_dir); poll_daemon.py:30 DEFAULT_GC_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 24*60*60, fired on the tick (100-102).
defects.impact: US-12 defines the one-shot CLI surface as export and import only; the project description says 'Continuous daemon operation, plus one-shot CLI subcommands for portable export and import'. No requirement mentions prune, a GC cadence, or reclaimed-bytes logging. A user-visible command and a background destructive timer ship with no acceptance criterion, so neither the cadence nor the command's arguments, exit codes, or (absent) dry-run can be verified or safely changed.

defects.title: The on-disk state and canonical formats do not match the documented layout
defects.evidence: state.json is written as {'schema_version': 1, 'records': {<id>: {'name','canonical_digest','surfaces':{<tool>:{'location':{'path'|'file'+'slot'},'content_digest'}}}}}. canonical_store.py:37 CANONICAL_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1; a file whose schema_version is not exactly 1 is quarantined (111-114). A third directory <state_dir>/quarantine/ holds <name>.<monotonic_ns>.<random>.corrupt.
defects.impact: docs/project_description.md documents a different layout as the contract: schema_version 4, key 'customization_artifacts' not 'records', per-tool 'agentic_tools' with 'digests'. US-10 AC-4 pins the state path as state.customization_artifacts[<id>].agentic_tools[<name>]. An install upgraded to the rebuild quarantines its schema-4 state and starts empty, re-projecting everything. The documented layout is the only description a recovery script has.

defects.title: An intent whose surfaces share one write file is refused every poll, forever
defects.evidence: `write_files = [target_file(s) for s in surfaces]; if len(set(write_files)) != len(write_files): raise IntentAbortError(...)`, called from project_canonical, adopt_new_artifact and rename_artifact; caught in execute_sync_plan/__init__.py:99 into execution.failed and retried identically next poll.
defects.impact: No requirement covers it. US-06 AC-6 (cited in the docstring) is about atomicity across conflict losers. US-04 AC-5 and US-03 AC-8 define refusals for slug collisions between DIFFERENT artifacts and require a structured error naming the colliding ids — this is one artifact with two surfaces, a different condition with a less informative outcome. A reasonable configuration (two tools anchored under ~/.gemini) stalls permanently with no diagnosis.

defects.title: Writing an MCP slot replaces any non-object value at the map path, discarding it unarchived
defects.evidence: `child = node.get(key); if not isinstance(child, dict): child = {}; node[key] = child`, justified in comment as 'loses no artifact data — it self-heals a structurally-broken shared file'.
defects.impact: A user's `mcpServers: null`, `mcp: "disabled"`, or a list at that key is deleted with no archive entry and no warning. The integration protocol requires keys outside map_key_path be preserved byte-for-byte but is silent on the map key itself holding something unexpected; NFR-01 forbids losing user-authored content 'under any operation'; US-05 AC-1 would require archiving anything displaced. The 'loses no artifact data' justification concerns MANAGED artifacts; the discarded value is user-authored config.

defects.title: An @import chain deeper than ten levels freezes the rules artifact
defects.evidence: _MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH = 10; `if _depth > _MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH: raise RulesImportError('rules @import nesting exceeds maximum depth')`; read_tool_surfaces.py:195-196 turns it into ParseFailure.
defects.impact: US-15 AC-1 requires transitive depth-first resolution with no stated bound. US-15 AC-4 enumerates exactly three failure cases — missing/unreadable file, file outside the rules directory, import cycle — and a depth cap is none of them. Cycles are already caught separately by _seen_targets, so the cap protects against nothing that is not already handled.

defects.title: A non-canonical but valid UUID is treated as absent, so a new id is minted and the file rewritten
defects.evidence: `if parsed.version != 4 or str(parsed) != value: raise InvalidArtifactId(...)`. recover_identity.py:75-81 swallows that into False, so _recover_id returns None -> AdoptNewArtifact -> mint_artifact_id(). An uppercase UUID, a brace-wrapped UUID, or a UUIDv1/v7 is rejected.
defects.impact: FR-11 requires that when the id tag 'is present and well-formed' the daemon 'shall not mint a new id, and shall not misattribute the artifact'. An uppercase spelling of the same UUID is arguably well-formed. Case-normalising a UUID by hand causes an identity split: a fresh id is minted, the artifact re-adopted, and the two copies can then collide by slug. FR-11's guarantee has an unwritten exception.

defects.title: OS sidecar files inside a skill folder are silently excluded from sync and deleted on the target
defects.evidence: _IGNORED_TREE_NAMES = frozenset({'.DS_Store'}), _IGNORED_TREE_PREFIXES = ('._',); read_auxiliary_files skips any path with a matching part. Module docstring justifies it as 'The legacy tree excluded these too; keeping the rule preserves that behaviour across cutover.'
defects.impact: US-01 AC-9 states the opposite without exception: 'When ANY file inside the folder is added, modified, moved, or deleted ... Auxiliary files are propagated verbatim.' A user file legitimately named ._template is invisible to sync and is destroyed on the target by the folder swap, since the staged tree is built only from the canonical. The exclusion set is also the kind of list that grows silently unless the rule is written down.

defects.title: The canonical rewrites the user's environment-variable reference syntax
defects.evidence: `for field in ('env','auth','headers'): changes[field] = _restyle_env_map(changes[field], _CANONICAL_ENV_STYLE)`; _ENV_REFERENCE_TOKEN_PATTERN matches ${env:N}, ${N} and {env:N} interchangeably; render.py restyles with spelling.env_reference_style, a single per-tool constant rather than the observed spelling.
defects.impact: NFR-06 requires round-trip preserve 'the original bytes on the source'. A user who wrote $TOKEN or {env:TOKEN} in a Claude config gets ${TOKEN} written back. The same dialect carefully preserves observed FIELD spellings via per_tool_only/_record_alias — the mechanism simply is not applied to VALUE syntax. The tests assert the canonical style rather than the authored one, so they cannot catch it.

defects.title: The MCP dialect rejects a range of well-formed slots as malformed, freezing the artifact
defects.evidence: Five independent checks raise MalformedSurfaceError: two spellings of one alias family (url + httpUrl), mixed stdio/http fields, command-as-array with args, a boolean or float timeout, and any slot value that is not JSON-representable (an unquoted TOML date in Codex's config.toml). Twelve-plus tests pin them.
defects.impact: The integration protocol lists the canonical fields and per-tool aliases and says only 'On a malformed slot, the artifact is skipped with a structured warning'. It never defines which field combinations are malformed, and it expects tools to spell fields differently. FR-11 authorises freezing on malformed metadata but leaves malformed undefined; here it is strict enough to reject configurations the tools themselves load fine.

defects.title: A corrupt state.json is quarantined and the daemon restarts from an empty state
defects.evidence: `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as error: quarantine_corrupt_file(...); return SyncState()`. _record_from_dict raises on any missing key, so strictness is deliberate. Pinned by test_sync_state_store.py::test_a_record_missing_required_keys_is_quarantined.
defects.impact: US-09 AC-4 specifies quarantine-and-rebuild for exactly one artefact — THE CANONICAL — not state.json. US-09 AC-3 says state lost from a clobbered write 'is recomputed from disk on the next poll', recomputed rather than discarded wholesale. One damaged byte triggers a full-library re-projection and a burst of archive entries on every tool. Whether state.json is disposable is a recovery-semantics decision nobody wrote down.

defects.title: Archive entry names carry a random token, so they do not match the documented archive layout
defects.evidence: `unique_token = uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]; timestamp = ...strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S-%fZ'); return side_dir / f'{entry_name}.{unique_token}.{timestamp}'`. The GC parses only the final dot-segment, which makes the token position load-bearing.
defects.impact: US-05 AC-1 gives the layout as a literal contract: archive/<artifact_id>/<tool_name>/<original-filename>.<ISO-UTC-timestamp>, repeated verbatim in US-03 AC-1, US-06 AC-1 and the integration protocol. US-05's Notes name the timestamp itself as the collision remedy. The archive layout is the user's documented recovery interface; a glob or sort written against the documented pattern misses or misorders every real entry.

defects.title: The configuration file contract — location, required table, and keys — is undefined in the spec
defects.evidence: Reads <config-dir>/agents-sync/config.toml and requires a top-level [agents-sync] table: `if _CONFIG_TABLE_KEY not in data: raise ConfigurationError(...)`. Honours exactly three settings plus one path-override key per surface. No per-tool enable/disable key exists.
defects.impact: US-07 AC-7 presupposes a config file and names two of its defects but never states where it lives, what its table is called, or what keys exist. US-10 AC-2 requires a matching [agentic_tools.<name>] config block — a nested shape the code does not implement — and US-10 AC-9 requires an `enabled = false` key that does not exist. The single interface the user configures the product through is defined only by its implementation.

defects.title: Transient I/O errors — including every PermissionError — are retried six times inside the poll
defects.evidence: _RETRY_ATTEMPTS=6, _RETRY_BASE_DELAY_SECONDS=0.02, _RETRY_MAX_DELAY_SECONDS=0.30, jittered by random.uniform(0.7,1.3); _is_transient_error: `if isinstance(error, PermissionError): return True` on every platform.
defects.impact: NFR-04 and US-07 AC-3 promise recovery BETWEEN polls, not retries within one. US-01 AC-11 and US-05 AC-4 treat 'permission denied' as a failure to report and re-attempt next poll — the code instead treats it as transient and blocks ~1s per operation. NFR-02's latency guarantee and NFR-09's linearity bound are both invisible to a sleeping retry loop.

defects.title: Slug derivation invents names: a shared placeholder for unnameable artifacts, an -item suffix for Windows device names
defects.evidence: _PLACEHOLDER_SLUG = 'converted'; `if not slug: return _PLACEHOLDER_SLUG`; `if slug.upper() in _WINDOWS_RESERVED_BASENAMES: return f'{slug}-item'`. candidate_key pairs the kind with this slug, so the slug is the reconciliation key.
defects.impact: The glossary defines Slug only as 'the filesystem-friendly form of a name'; the integration protocol lists filename-character restrictions as a POSSIBLE FUTURE layout flag, i.e. explicitly not yet specified. A user with purely CJK or emoji artifact names gets every such artifact collapsed onto the single key 'converted' and rejected as a collision (US-03 AC-8), which reads as a bug with no spec to appeal to.

defects.title: A surface whose stat() races loses every freshness tiebreak by being dated to the epoch
defects.evidence: `try: return path.stat().st_mtime except OSError: return 0.0`, docstring: 'The epoch sentinel makes the racing surface lose any freshest-content tiebreak this poll.' freshest() sorts on -modified_time (winner_selection.py:28-35). Same code as CD-0005, filed there as a silent swallow; the spec angle is separate.
defects.impact: US-06 AC-1 defines the winner as 'the changed agentic_tool with the most recent mtime' and AC-4 defines the tie-break by tool name; neither contemplates an unreadable mtime. No requirement says an unstattable surface should be deemed oldest rather than excluded or deferred, and NFR-13 would require a structured report of the condition; none is emitted.

defects.title: US-05 AC-1 demands an archive entry on every ordinary propagation that US-06 AC-2 and NFR-07 both forbid
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: An agent is managed on claude and codex, byte-identical. The user edits it on claude only. Exactly one tool is in the changed set, so US-06 AC-2 governs and says 'no archive entry is written for the unchanged agentic_tools'. But codex's prior bytes are the PREVIOUS projection — reproducible from the previous canonical, not the current one — so US-05 AC-1's Given also holds and demands an archive entry. US-05 AC-3 does not settle it: it exempts only content byte-equal to a render of the CURRENT canonical.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: content_intents.py:77-83 follows US-05 AC-1 and archives on every propagated edit; the only skip is byte-identity: `if new_text == prior_text and auxiliary_files_already_on_disk(...): continue` then `if prior_text is not None: archive_copy(...)`. A stale-but-different projection is always archived.
defects.impact: Every ordinary edit writes N-1 archive copies of daemon-generated projections containing no user-authored content — exactly what NFR-07 exists to prevent. On 200 artifacts across 5 tools routine editing generates thousands of entries, and the tiered GC then exists mainly to clean up entries the spec says should never have been created. It also destroys 'is there an archive entry?' as a signal that something was at risk.
defects.which_side_loses: US-06 AC-2 and NFR-07

defects.title: US-11 AC-9 makes a deliberate multi-artifact deletion unexpressible, and the code then neither removes nor restores
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: The user cleans house: one `rm` deletes three obsolete skills from ~/.claude/skills/. All three are recorded for claude and vanish inside one 2-second poll. AC-9 calls that a glitch and refuses the removal; FR-03 ('shall observe ... removals') and NFR-17 ('shall adapt to the user ... removing ... without requiring any further interaction') require it to be honoured. There is no gesture for 'delete these three' — deleting one poll apart is the only supported one, and nothing says so.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: compute_sync_plan.py:130-137 rewrites RemoveArtifact to ReprojectCanonical for glitched tools. But the executor's reproject targets come from recorded_targets, which skips any recorded location with no observation (_shared.py:130-139: 'A recorded location without an observation is skipped'). The vanished tool is therefore never written to. Net effect every poll, forever: no removal, no restoration, state still recording files that do not exist.
defects.impact: A bulk deletion is silently ignored on the deleting tool and never propagated, while copies on every other tool live on. The artifact enters permanent limbo and the daemon re-decides the same non-action every poll. Pairs with CD-0001, which is the same rule's other side: delete exactly one and it is destroyed everywhere; delete three and nothing happens, ever.
defects.which_side_loses: FR-03 and NFR-17 on the spec; in the code BOTH sides lose — neither removed nor restored

defects.title: US-11 AC-1 makes a tool wholly unavailable if any one per-type directory is missing, which no ordinary install survives
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: Ordinary installs: a user runs Claude Code but never created ~/.claude/skills/, or runs Cursor with no ~/.cursor/mcp.json (note mcp_server's root is a FILE, which the status definition 'directory reachable' cannot even describe). Under AC-1 the whole tool is unavailable, so US-01 AC-6 and US-06 AC-5 exclude it from agents, rules and slash_commands too, and US-07 AC-5 means two such tools stop all destructive operations.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: sync_once.py:57-58 implements the exact opposite: `if any(directory.exists() for directory in directories): available += 1`. Reachability is judged per surface instead, and reconcile_known.py:164-167 argues explicitly against AC-1's granularity. read_tool_surfaces.py:362-369 refuses to create an absent directory, so a missing skills/ simply never receives projections. The protocol's partial_availability model is what is implemented in spirit, but it appears in no story or requirement.
defects.impact: The spec's central safety concept — tool status — is defined at a granularity the system cannot use, so every criterion phrased over 'the agentic_tool's status' (US-01 AC-6, US-06 AC-5, US-11 AC-2/4/7, US-07 AC-5) is untestable against the implementation. The two readings also differ on FR-04's safety-critical question: whether a tool may source a removal signal when only some directories are readable. Overlaps CD-0025.
defects.which_side_loses: US-11 AC-1 and the three-status glossary model

defects.title: US-07 AC-5's two-tool freeze cancels FR-16, US-12 AC-5 and US-11 AC-8 on exactly the machine they were written for
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: The literal US-12 scenario: restore your library onto a new laptop with only Claude Code installed. available_tool_count == 1. FR-16 and US-12 AC-5 require the imported canonicals to be adopted and projected onto claude; US-07 AC-5 forbids adoption until a second tool appears. US-11 AC-8's heal path ('a freshly imported artifact on zero agentic_tools') is named in the same breath and is likewise adoption.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: US-07 AC-5 wins. compute_sync_plan.py:46-53 puts ADOPT_NEW_ARTIFACT, ABSORB_INTO_MANAGED, PROJECT_TO_TOOLS, RENAME_ARTIFACT and REMOVE_ARTIFACT in _DESTRUCTIVE_KINDS; lines 106-107 drop them all below the threshold. REPROJECT_CANONICAL survives, so the guard admits tool-file writes anyway — itself 'propagation' under AC-5's wording (test_compute_sync_plan.py:555 asserts this deliberately).
defects.impact: `agents-sync import` on a one-tool machine reports success and writes canonicals that never reach disk, with no error and no log line explaining why. The restored library is invisible until a second tool happens to be installed. The guard also fails to be the clean invariant it claims, since reprojection writes tool files below the threshold.
defects.which_side_loses: FR-16, US-12 AC-5 and US-11 AC-8

defects.title: US-01 AC-8 prescribes a folder-swap mechanism that cannot deliver the visibility guarantee it and NFR-03 assert
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: Any skill propagation. The prescribed two-rename sequence (rename target to .old, rename .tmp into place) has a window in which the skill folder does not exist, so a tool enumerating ~/.claude/skills/ during it sees the skill missing — the state the same criterion forbids. POSIX offers no portable atomic replace of a non-empty directory, so the mechanism AC-8 mandates and the property AC-8 asserts cannot both hold.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: atomic_file_writer.py:112-117 implements the prescribed mechanism and documents the hole rather than the promise: 'The two renames leave a bounded transient window with no target (directories have no exchange primitive)'. Separately AC-8's final clause is simply not done: line 128 does `retry_transient_io(lambda: shutil.rmtree(backup_dir))` where AC-8 says 'the .old tree is archived', and project_canonical archives only SKILL.md (content_intents.py:82), never the auxiliary files it is about to replace.
defects.impact: A load-bearing safety requirement (NFR-03) is stated in a form no folder implementation can satisfy, so it can only be waived informally in a code comment. And because AC-8 buried the archive obligation inside a mechanism description, the one part that genuinely protects user data was dropped without any criterion visibly failing — a user-edited auxiliary file displaced by a folder swap is destroyed with no archive copy, breaching NFR-01.
defects.which_side_loses: both — the visibility clause is unachievable as specified, and the archive clause is unimplemented

defects.title: 'Sibling slots preserved byte-for-byte' cannot coexist with the read-modify-write merge the same section prescribes
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: The user has one MCP server synced to Codex, whose shared file ~/.codex/config.toml is a hand-maintained config with comments, blank-line grouping and a chosen key order, holding much more than [mcp_servers]. The daemon adds one slot. A merge going through a value-level parse and re-emit cannot return the surrounding bytes unchanged; only a byte-level splice could. Same for a JSONC mcp-config.json, and for ~/.claude.json, which carries large amounts of unrelated Claude Code state.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: structured_text.py:8-9 states it: 'Round-trip preserves key order and data; it does not preserve comments.' TOML is re-emitted by a hand-rolled _emit_toml_table (114-127) that reorders scalars before tables and normalises every scalar. JSONC is worse than lossy: _deserialize_json (99) uses json.loads, so a comment makes the whole file malformed and every slot in it freezes.
defects.impact: The daemon silently rewrites a hand-maintained tool config the first time it touches one MCP slot, and the archive contract deliberately excludes exactly the bytes lost — US-13 AC-7 says the bytes outside the slot's map_key_path entry are never archived. The criterion as written also cannot be satisfied by any implementation, so it can never gate the work.
defects.which_side_loses: US-13 AC-3 and the protocol's byte-for-byte clause; NFR-01 with them

defects.title: FR-11's whole-artifact freeze and FR-02's fault isolation give opposite answers when one tool's copy is malformed and another's was edited
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: A skill exists on claude, codex and cursor. Months ago the user hand-edited ~/.claude/skills/formatter/SKILL.md and left the YAML front matter broken; the id line is intact so the artifact is still identified. Today they edit the same skill on codex. FR-02 and US-06 AC-2 say the codex edit propagates to cursor (the failure is confined to claude); FR-11 and US-03 AC-11 say the whole artifact is frozen and nothing syncs anywhere.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: FR-11 wins, and the freeze triggers on any surface for any reason. reconcile_known.py:60-61: `if any(isinstance(observation.parsed, ParseFailure) for observation in observations): return (FreezeArtifact(artifact_id),)` — first in the pipeline, short-circuiting the content rule. The executor merely records the id, and src_new emits no warning at all, so NFR-13's 'structured warning' half of FR-11 is absent.
defects.impact: One stale broken file on one tool silently suspends synchronisation of that artifact across every tool, indefinitely, with no diagnostic in the rebuild. The user sees edits on a healthy tool simply not propagating. Which behaviour is intended is genuinely undecided — FR-02's own wording ('continue processing the other agentic_tools') reads as the opposite of FR-11's freeze.
defects.which_side_loses: FR-02 and US-06 AC-2

defects.title: US-14 AC-5's create-name and FR-10's 'preferring AGENTS.md' name different files, and the code follows FR-10
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: A user keeps global rules in ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and has Claude Code installed with neither ~/.claude/AGENTS.md nor ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. The rules artifact is projected onto claude. AC-5 says create CLAUDE.md; the code creates AGENTS.md, citing FR-10. FR-10 says nothing about which name to use when CREATING a file, and the protocol puts the answer in a separate field: 'fixed_file_name is the create-name used when rendering a fresh file. Claude declares candidate_file_names=(AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) with create-name CLAUDE.md'.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: read_tool_surfaces.py:373-375 returns candidate_filenames[0] with a comment citing FR-10. SurfaceRecipe (tool_definition.py:85) has no create-name field at all — the protocol's fixed_file_name has no counterpart — and claude.py:63 declares only candidate_filenames.
defects.impact: Claude Code does not natively load AGENTS.md the way CLAUDE.md is loaded, which is the entire rationale AC-5 states. A user whose rules are propagated onto claude gets a file the tool may ignore, so the sync appears to have silently done nothing. Duplicate of CD-0031 from pass 1, reached independently from the spec direction and adding the protocol's fixed_file_name evidence.
defects.which_side_loses: US-14 AC-5, one of six criteria the story marks [x] and 'Status: Done (v0.5)'

defects.title: US-03 never covers two new artifacts sharing one reconciliation key on the SAME tool, and AC-4's counting rule forces a destructive merge
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: Two distinct unmanaged agent files in ONE directory whose names slugify identically: ~/.claude/agents/code-review.md with `name: Code Review` and ~/.claude/agents/review.md with `name: code_review`. Or, far more commonly, two agent files with no name field, which both slug to the placeholder. AC-3's Given needs two TOOLS; AC-8's needs already-MANAGED artifacts; neither applies. AC-4's counting rule ('the total number created equals the number of distinct reconciliation keys') says one artifact must result.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: adopt_candidates.py:26-36 groups purely on candidate_key(kind, name) with no tool distinction; _adopt picks the freshest as source and puts the other in others. identity_intents.py:58-74 then writes the winner's canonical into EVERY surface in the group, stamping both files with one minted id. reject_shared_write_file does not fire because the paths differ. The nameless case is guaranteed by artifact_naming.py:26,39-40 — _PLACEHOLDER_SLUG = 'converted'.
defects.impact: Two different user-authored agents silently become two copies of one agent sharing one id. The losing content survives only in the archive, and the user's second file now contains someone else's agent. The placeholder-slug path makes this reachable with no exotic naming: any tool whose format derives the name from the filename (the protocol names opencode agents) parses to an empty name in src_new and lands every such artifact on the same key.
defects.which_side_loses: undecidable — no criterion covers it; AC-4 read literally endorses the destructive merge, against NFR-01

defects.title: US-01 AC-5's comment-preservation cannot hold on a restore, because NFR-16 requires only fields and values in the canonical
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: NFR-16's fidelity clause is scoped to 'every field and value'; comments are neither, so nothing requires the canonical to carry them. AC-5 is scoped to any rewrite. They collide whenever a file is produced with no prior copy on disk to seed the formatting — US-11 AC-9's restore-from-canonical, and US-11 AC-8's projection onto a tool that lost its copy. Concretely: front matter carrying `# keep this model, the cheaper one hallucinates` is restored without the comment, and no archive entry exists because nothing on disk was displaced.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: markdown_frontmatter.py:146 returns dict(loaded) from the ruamel round-trip load, discarding comment attachments before the canonical is built; render re-attaches them only via _base_frontmatter(prior_text) (149-160). content_intents.py:75 supplies prior_text only if the file exists — for a vanished or never-present file that is None, so the file is rebuilt bare.
defects.impact: The spec promises formatting fidelity unconditionally but only funds it for the in-place-rewrite path. Any recovery path — the one users most need to trust — silently strips their annotations. It also makes AC-5 untestable as a general property: it can only be demonstrated on the one path that happens to have a prior file.
defects.which_side_loses: US-01 AC-5 on every from-canonical write; NFR-01 with it

defects.title: Global-rules artifacts have two incompatible identities: the fixed name 'global' and the frontmatter-declared slug
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: A user puts `name: house-style` in front matter at the top of ~/.claude/AGENTS.md — legal, since that is how customization_artifact_id is injected. Its identity is now 'global' per one clause and 'house-style' per the other. Meanwhile ~/.codex/AGENTS.md has no front matter and is 'global'. Two reconciliation keys, but on every global-rules tool both project to the same single file path, because the rules layout has one file per tool and its name does not depend on the slug.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: read_tool_surfaces.py:176-178 lets a declared name win over the recipe default (test_read_tool_surfaces.py:451 pins it). But _projection_location (373-375) ignores the slug for Layout.RULES_FILE and returns candidate_filenames[0]. So two rules artifacts with different names target the same path on the same tool, and the planner's collision guard cannot see it: _index_managed_keys (compute_sync_plan.py:143-159) keys on (kind, slug), not on the write path.
defects.impact: Two managed artifacts can be projected onto one file with no collision rejection — the situation US-03 AC-8 and US-04 AC-5 exist to prevent. The result is a rules file that flips content between polls plus an archive entry per flip. The ambiguity is entirely in the spec: nothing says whether a global-rules file's name field is authoritative or ignored.
defects.which_side_loses: undecidable from the spec; in the code both artifacts survive and fight over one file

defects.title: No criterion covers a removal on one tool colliding with an edit on another in the same poll
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: A skill is on claude and codex. Within one 2-second poll the user deletes it on claude and saves an edit to it on codex. One recorded surface has vanished and one has changed. US-05 AC-2 says propagate the removal; US-06 AC-2 says propagate the codex edit to claude. Both Givens hold and their Thens are mutually exclusive. Nothing orders them, and the glossary's changed-set definition ('digest differs from the last_written digest') has no value for a deleted file.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: Removal wins unconditionally by pipeline order. reconcile_known.py:64-68 returns (RemoveArtifact(artifact_id),) before `changed` is even computed; the module docstring states it: 'remove if a recorded tool's surface vanished (US-11, short-circuiting content)'. The codex edit is archived and then deleted.
defects.impact: A just-saved edit is deleted from disk because of a deletion the user performed on a different tool seconds earlier. The bytes survive only in the archive, and nothing is logged. The opposite resolution — treating the fresher edit as a resurrection — is equally defensible, which is exactly why the spec needs to say.
defects.which_side_loses: US-06 AC-2, by an ordering decision made in code and stated nowhere

defects.title: NFR-07 is titled 'bounded archive growth' but states only a creation rule, leaving the archive-deleting GC unauthorised
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: NFR-07's body constrains only when entries are CREATED; it authorises no deletion, and a creation rule alone bounds nothing. Meanwhile the implementation deletes archived bytes. Concrete: a user deletes a skill, so the removal moves its only remaining copy into the archive; thirteen months later the entry is gone. Sooner: if five entries land for one artifact/tool on one day, only four survive past day 7 and one past day 30.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: artifact_archive.py:36-41 implements a tiered deletion policy and cites NFR-07 as its authority — KEEP_ALL_WITHIN_DAYS=7, DOWNSAMPLE_DAYS=30, RETAIN_DAYS=365, KEEP_PER_DAY_RECENT=4, KEEP_PER_DAY_OLD=1. _apply_tiered_policy hands anything older than 365 days to _remove_entry, which rmtrees or unlinks it. The daemon runs it on a daily tick.
defects.impact: The archive is the sole recovery mechanism behind the project's third goal ('No user-authored content is ever destroyed'), and its retention policy is set entirely by five constants with no requirement to check them against. The requirement's title also promises a bound its body does not deliver, so a reviewer reading NFR-07 alone would believe growth is capped. Duplicate of CD-0026 from pass 1, reached from the spec side.
defects.which_side_loses: undecidable as written — read strictly, NFR-07 forbids the deletion, in which case US-05 and NFR-01 lose to unspecified behaviour

defects.title: The mtime tiebreaker is specified at one-second precision while the glossary defines the timestamp as a float
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: The user edits the same agent on claude at 10:00:00.2 and on codex at 10:00:00.7, both inside one 2-second poll — the exact scenario US-06 exists for, since sub-second separation is what 'edited in the same poll' means. At one-second precision the mtimes are identical, so AC-4 requires the lexicographic winner (claude) and a `WARN tied-mtime` line. At float precision codex is simply fresher and AC-1 applies with no warning. Two criteria, two winners, two log outcomes, one event.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: winner_selection.py:34-35 compares full float mtimes: `return (-observation.modified_time, tool)` over path.stat().st_mtime. The tie is broken by name only on exact float equality, so AC-4's tie branch is effectively unreachable, and src_new emits no log line anywhere in the planner or executor — grep for a tied-mtime warning returns nothing.
defects.impact: The one criterion that makes conflict resolution auditable — telling the user their two edits were indistinguishable and why one was chosen — cannot fire, so a lost edit looks like a silent overwrite. The criterion cannot be tested as written without deliberately choosing the reading the implementation rejects.
defects.which_side_loses: US-06 AC-4 and US-03 AC-7

defects.title: US-15's framework-specific hold-back overrides FR-07 with no parent requirement, and is dead code in the rebuild
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: Two collisions. (1) Global rules files routinely mention tool directories — the phrase ~/.claude/skills is enough — so under AC-6 the whole file is held back and never synced anywhere, while FR-07 says unconditionally that rules sync across every supporting tool. The story admits the gap: 'A new FR formalising import resolution + the framework-specific egress guard should be cascaded ... to give AC-1..AC-7 a parent requirement.' (2) The user edits rules on claude and codex in one poll; claude wins; codex's file mentions .cursor/, so AC-7 protects it from overwrite while US-06 AC-1 requires every loser to be overwritten and AC-6 requires the loser set to be all-or-nothing.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: In the rebuild the guard is DEAD CODE, so FR-07 wins and the hold-back does not happen: detect_framework_specific is defined at global_rules.py:41 and has no caller anywhere in src_new or tests_new, while its docstring still claims 'The read phase's egress guard (S17-S19) calls it'. In legacy src/ the guard IS wired (US-15 records adoption/privacy_gate.py), so the two trees resolve the same criteria oppositely.
defects.impact: Seven criteria marked [x] Implemented govern whether global rules propagate at all, and they contradict the requirement saying they must, with the story itself noting no parent requirement exists. Because the two trees behave oppositely, CUTTING OVER SILENTLY FLIPS THE BEHAVIOUR: rules files previously held back will start propagating Claude-only paths into Codex and opencode, which US-16's notes call incorrect behaviour. The dead detect_framework_specific also belongs to 2.b as dead-code.
defects.which_side_loses: FR-07 under the spec as written; in src_new, AC-6 and AC-7

defects.title: Nothing says what state an already-managed artifact is left in when secrets_refused blocks it
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: 'Not adopted' only has meaning for a NEW artifact. The uncovered reachable state: an mcp_server artifact already managed and synced across claude, codex and cursor, and the user pastes a literal API key into the cursor slot. It cannot be 'not adopted' — it is already adopted. Cursor now holds a version the other two will never receive, the canonical still holds the old clean version, and no criterion says whether the artifact is frozen, reverted, left divergent, or reported once versus every poll.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: Leaves it permanently divergent and re-attempts forever. content_intents.py:42-44 calls enforce_secret_policy inside absorb_tool_edit, which raises SecretLeakError; execute_sync_plan/__init__.py:96-98 catches it and appends the label to `blocked` — no canonical write, no record update. `blocked` is not even reported by the daemon loop (poll_daemon.py logs only result.failed). Because the record's digest is never updated, the surface is 'changed' again next poll, so the refusal recurs every 2 seconds, silently, forever.
defects.impact: The default policy's most likely real-world trigger — pasting a key into an already-synced server config — is the case the spec does not describe. The user gets no error, no propagation, and a permanently divergent artifact, with no specified way out other than editing the file back.
defects.which_side_loses: undecidable — no criterion applies; NFR-15's error-reporting obligation loses in practice

defects.title: US-12 AC-2's 'single atomic read of the canonical store at one moment' has two readings and no test can distinguish them
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: Reading (a): each entry is read atomically, one at a time. Reading (b): the whole store is captured as of one instant. They differ exactly under the criterion's own Given — a live daemon. With (a) the daemon can absorb an edit to artifact B after the export read artifact A, so the export contains A-before and B-after, a combination that existed at no single moment. With (b) that is forbidden, but nothing in the design (no lock, per US-09) can deliver it.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: Implements reading (a) and silently redefines the criterion to match. portable_library/_export.py:6-8: 'each canonical store file's bytes are read once for a coherent point-in-time snapshot of THAT ENTRY' — the per-entry qualifier is the implementation's, not the criterion's. _collect_entries (111-134) loops over list_canonical_ids reading one file per iteration, with no snapshot and no barrier against a concurrent save_canonical.
defects.impact: The one acceptance criterion protecting export-under-load is unverifiable, so a torn cross-artifact export ships as conforming. That matters because FR-15 makes the mirror-image promise for import in a form that IS testable — the two halves of the same concurrency story are held to different standards.
defects.which_side_loses: undecidable — the criterion cannot be falsified as written, so it gates nothing

defects.title: No criterion covers a single unreadable artifact file, nor names the condition under which the daemon may exit runtime-failure
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: Two adjacent holes. (1) A single artifact file becomes unreadable — chmod 000 on one agent file, an I/O error, a binary file dropped into agents/. The directory is fine (so US-11 AC-6, scoped to a directory, does not apply) and the metadata is not malformed (so FR-11 does not apply); the file simply cannot be read. (2) A whole-poll exception recurs — the state directory becomes read-only, or $HOME is briefly unmounted. US-07 AC-3 promises recovery with no bound; NFR-10 implies exiting is sometimes right but no criterion says after how many failures or which qualify.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: (1) read_tool_surfaces.py:214-219 returns ParseFailure('unreadable surface: ...') for OSError/UnicodeDecodeError, which reconcile_known.py:60-61 converts to a whole-artifact freeze — the same fate as malformed metadata, with no log. (2) poll_daemon.py:28 DEFAULT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 5, lines 94-95 return EXIT_RUNTIME_FAILURE — ten seconds at the default interval.
defects.impact: A ten-second blip — an unmounted home directory, a laptop resuming from sleep — is enough to stop the daemon permanently on a system whose supervisor does not restart on exit code 1, the opposite of NFR-17's unattended promise, and no criterion authorises or bounds it. For the unreadable file, the chosen behaviour (freeze on every tool) is the most disruptive of the three plausible readings and was never agreed.
defects.which_side_loses: undecidable for (1); for (2) US-07 AC-3 and NFR-17 lose to an unspecified threshold

defects.title: US-09 AC-4 and US-05 AC-5 send a canonical leaving the store to two different, mutually exclusive destinations
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: A quarantine IS a drop: the record leaves the canonical store. US-05 AC-5's Given is written as a general rule over any such drop ('an operation drops ... from the canonical store', with removal only as an e.g.) and states the general principle behind it, so it applies. US-09 AC-4 then explicitly forbids AC-5's destination — 'separate from the user-content archive'. A user recovering a canonical must know which of two locations to look in, and the spec gives contradictory answers for the corruption case.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: Follows AC-4 for corruption and AC-5 for removal, in two modules with no shared rule. canonical_store.py:142-145 _quarantine calls quarantine_corrupt_file (moving under store_dir/quarantine/), while identity_intents.py:154-157 does archive_move(state_dir, artifact_id, '_canonical', stored_canonical). Neither path logs anything in src_new, so AC-4's 'a structured error is logged' is also unmet.
defects.impact: Recovery is the entire purpose of both criteria and they disagree on where to look. The split also means the archive-retention GC, which only walks state_dir/archive, never touches quarantined canonicals, so the two classes of preserved data have different, unspecified lifetimes.
defects.which_side_loses: US-05 AC-5's claim to be the general no-rm rule for the canonical store

defects.title: US-10 AC-9's absolute logging silence for disabled tools contradicts NFR-12, two documents mis-cite it, and no disable mechanism exists
defects.evidence: THE SITUATION: Startup with `enabled = false` for codex. NFR-12 says every tool's status is logged once at startup ('startup counts as a transition'); AC-9 says nothing about this tool is ever logged. A user debugging 'why is codex not syncing?' gets silence under one and an answer under the other. Compounding it, both the US-11 status table and the protocol cite US-10 AC-7 for this behaviour — but AC-7 is the INCOHERENT INTEGRATION criterion whose Then is 'the daemon exits with the configuration-failure code'. Following the reference gives the opposite of the intended behaviour.  ||  WHAT THE CODE DOES: Neither: src_new has NO disable mechanism at all. runtime_config.load_runtime_config (114-140) validates only paths, poll interval, state path and secret policy — there is no `enabled` key anywhere in src_new, and ALL_TOOL_DEFINITIONS is consumed unconditionally. There is also no status logging of any kind, so NFR-12 is unimplemented too.
defects.impact: A user cannot turn a tool off at all in the rebuild, and if they could, the spec disagrees with itself about whether they would ever be told. The mis-citation is the more dangerous half: two normative documents point a future implementer at a criterion that says to exit with a configuration failure.
defects.which_side_loses: NFR-12 on the spec's own terms; in src_new both, since neither disabling nor status logging exists

passes.direction_note: Reconnaissance only — no source or test file was touched.
passes.note: Seed reconnaissance sweep — one subagent, briefed on the full flag catalogue and the whole scope, deliberately shallow and time-boxed. Returned 22 findings across 12 flag classes and reported no contamination. This is a sample, not an inventory: it satisfies no gate and makes no completeness claim. Its only purpose is to give every activity a non-empty denominator, so that activity 0's and 1.a's verification is not vacuous by construction.
